summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT) with hands-on embedded systems experience across STM32 bare-metal C, FreeRTOS, and sensor-integrated hardware platforms. Built and debugged firmware using interrupt-driven UART and I2C communication, closed-loop sensor feedback, and real-time state machine control on custom PCBs and microcontroller-driven systems. Comfortable working directly with hardware test stands, oscilloscopes, and logic analyzers to validate hardware-software interfaces end to end.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove for hands-free cursor control, integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with a Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth module to translate 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands via Python.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; debugged and resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Built a Cortex-M4 temperature monitoring firmware in embedded C with timer-synchronized sensing and real-time display.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver.
Programmed peripherals directly in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1); achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at a deterministic 1 Hz update rate; verified in Proteus.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used a Jetson-based vision pipeline to detect and track objects, sending control commands to an STM32 over UART.
Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART command handling and user override.
Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing and OLED distance visualization.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Implemented two-link inverse kinematics on an Arduino microcontroller in C++, driving five servos with range-gated, sensor-triggered contact detection for a vision-guided robotic arm.
Integrated dual VL53L0X time-of-flight sensors over a TCA9548A I2C multiplexer for contact-aware grasping, combining a camera range-gate with a 25mm gripper-triggered close threshold.

awards: 1st Prize, CanSat Workshop — Arduino Nano atmospheric data collection during free fall (2023)
Ranked 10th, Robocon — National-level robotics competition among 45 universities (2022)
